name: invariant_LiquidityAssetConservation
property: sum of USDe balances across ARM, market, adapter, feeCollector, actors and deployer equals USDe.totalSupply()
rationale: catches any bug where the ARM's transfer/transferFrom bookkeeping creates or destroys the liquidity asset

name: invariant_BaseAssetConservation
property: sum of sUSDe balances across ARM, adapter and actors equals sUSDe.totalSupply()
rationale: same conservation check for the base asset leg of swaps/adapter redemptions

name: invariant_ShareSupplyAccountedFor
property: sum of ARM LP-share balances across actors, the ARM contract itself (redeem escrow) and DEAD_ACCOUNT equals arm.totalSupply()
rationale: would catch LP shares leaking to an unexpected address (e.g. a mis-targeted _mint/_transfer in a future code path)

name: invariant_ReservedWithdrawLiquidityMatchesUnclaimedRequests
property: reservedWithdrawLiquidity == sum of request.assets over all unclaimed withdrawal requests, and arm.balanceOf(arm) == sum of request.shares over the same set
rationale: directly tests the core promise of claimRedeem/requestRedeem bookkeeping (reservation release and share-escrow burn) computed independently from on-chain state rather than mirrored, so a bug in either function's accounting would be caught

name: invariant_ClaimGateNeverBlocksABackedRequest
property: whenever a withdrawal request is matured and passes the ARM's own claim gate (request.queued <= claimable()), claimRedeem() must actually succeed
rationale: this is the deepest, most valuable property here: claimable()'s share-denominated FIFO gate is documented in the contract's own comments as having edge cases (non-liquid NAV growth without matching liquidity growth can shrink the share frontier). A handler probe actively attempts every gated-but-unclaimed request and flags any revert as a genuine solvency-gate failure, not just a benign happy-path call

name: invariant_TotalAssetsFloor
property: totalAssets() never returns less than MIN_TOTAL_SUPPLY (1e12)
rationale: sanity check on the explicit clamp in totalAssets(); also guards against any future refactor accidentally removing the clamp or introducing an underflow path

name: invariant_BaseAssetPriceBoundsHold
property: for the supported base asset, buyPrice < crossPrice <= sellPrice always
rationale: this spread is what guarantees discounted buys still add NAV to LPs and the ARM never sells base assets under its own valuation price; setPrices/setCrossPrice/addBaseAsset each enforce it locally but the invariant checks it survives arbitrary admin+swap interleavings

name: invariant_ClaimedSharesNeverExceedQueuedShares
rationale: basic FIFO-queue sanity: cumulative claims can never exceed cumulative requests
